A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 6 and appendices C–E report original ACSIncome, ACSPubCov, and CheXpert experiments, including proxy errors and fairness violations before and after adjustment.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and their measured proxy errors, fairness violations, and post-processing outcomes in Section 6 and appendices C–E.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same regression and multicalibration-boosting procedures. The proxy-based bounds and adjustment mechanisms are unchanged; revised theoretical guarantees and explanations do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same California ACSIncome and ACSPubCov tasks and CheXpert pleural-effusion prediction, with the same missing-sensitive-attribute scenarios. The newly explicit income cutoff describes the retained ACSPubCov population rather than establishing added coverage.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain the same unadjusted and proxy-adjusted models, including logistic regression, decision trees, Random Forests for ACS, and DenseNet-121 for CheXpert. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The stated ACS evaluation split, training/adjustment allocation, CheXpert split source, model configurations, and AE/ECE evaluation measures are retained. v3 does not document a replacement protocol; identifying the existing MC definition as an l1 notion does not change the metric.

E4.justification: The same analyses across sensitive groups and model families, including adjustment benefits and cases with negligible benefit, remain in Section 6 and Appendix E. No new ablation, sensitivity, robustness, or error analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging ACS results over five train/validation splits. Neither adds seed information, uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or a changed repeated-run reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the matched result plots retain the same outcomes. For example, both report the ACSIncome decision-tree multicalibration bound decreasing from approximately 0.21 to 0.13 after adjustment. Changes such as 0.0269 to 0.027 are equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: Lemma 4.1 newly asserts tightness, and Appendix B.1 adds explicit attaining-distribution constructions for both MA and MC bounds in both MSE/proxy-error regimes. v1 only established the inequalities. Theorem 5.3 also changes the stated iteration bound from T < 4/alpha^4 to T < 4/alpha^2.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain proxy-based fairness bounds and their reduction through post-processing. The conclusion modestly narrows the promise from being able to 'certify and correct' MA/MC to providing certificates and strengthening them, emphasizing improvement of guarantees.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces the assertion that boosting produces lower MSE with the qualification that MSE is close and potentially lower. Appendix B.1 newly distinguishes existence-based tightness from bounds conditioned on full observed marginals, explaining that additional information could permit tighter bounds through Frechet inequalities.

D1.justification: Section 6 newly supplies an experiment-code repository link. Section 6.1.2 also specifies the retained ACSPubCov low-income threshold as below $30,000. These improve access information and documentation without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds medical-bias references by Li et al. and Yi et al., discusses MC variants, and connects possible tighter bounds to existing Frechet-based work. The main positioning relative to parity-based proxy fairness remains intact; the renamed Glocker citation refers to the same work.

P1.justification: Local prose edits clarify terminology and increase use of MA/MC abbreviations. Section 2 is retitled, Appendix E gains subsections, and publication and acknowledgement text is added. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The four main figures are regrouped into two displays with paired subfigures. Throughout Appendix E, plots and captions become narrower centered blocks, while collective captions become subsection headings. The contents are compressed onto the title page. This substantially changes visual presentation without adding result plots.

improvement.justification: The added tightness constructions strengthen the characterization of the central bounds, while the more cautious MSE discussion and explicit tightness limitation improve interpretation. The code link also improves reproducibility information. Smaller plots reduce readability, but the theoretical and documentation gains support a modest net improvement.
